items.title: Section: Fascicle 50 Opens — The Ten Powers Synthesised Through Seven Angles

items.zh: 如是別釋佛十力已，今當總辨。嗢拕南曰：自性、與分別、不共、亦平等、作業、及次第、差別最為後。
items.en:
Within the basic section, the Bodhisattva Stage, the third yoga foundation of ultimate practice, the second part of the fifth chapter, the chapter on establishment.
Second, general synthesis; first, stating the list; first, the summary verse. Having thus individually explained the Tathāgata's ten powers, we now synthesise them as a whole. The summary verse states: nature and differentiation, exclusivity and also equality, function and sequence, distinction explained last.

items.title: Section: The First Angle — Wisdom Alone Is Named the Very Nature of the Ten Powers

items.zh: 如是所說如來十力，所有自性應當了知，所有分別應當了知，所有不共應當了知，所有平等應當了知，所有作業應當了知，所有次第應當了知，所有差別應當了知。由是七相，應知如來十力略義。云何如來十力自性？謂總五根為其自性。由慧勝故，且說十力慧為自性。所以但言處非處智力，不言信力、不言餘力。如處非處智力，如是餘力，當知亦爾。是名如來十力自性。
items.en:
Second, the prose. Regarding the Tathāgata's ten powers as explained: their nature should be understood, their differentiation should be understood, their exclusivity should be understood, their equality should be understood, their function should be understood, their sequence should be understood, their distinction should be understood. By these seven characteristics, the essential meaning of the Tathāgata's ten powers should be known.
Second, explaining in turn; first, nature; first, posing the question. What is the nature of the Tathāgata's ten powers?
Second, explaining; first, stating the essential nature. In general, the five faculties constitute their nature; but because wisdom is foremost, it is said that wisdom is the nature of the ten powers.
Second, showing what is foremost; first, citing the first. This is why it is said only "the power of wisdom regarding what is possible and impossible," not "the power of faith" nor any other faculty's power.
Second, extending to the rest. As with the power of wisdom regarding what is possible and impossible, so too should the remaining powers be understood.
Third, concluding. This is called the nature of the Tathāgata's ten powers.

items.title: Section: The Second Angle — Immeasurable Through Time, Through Kind, and Through Every Being's Own Continuity

items.zh: 云何如來十力分別？謂若略說，由三分別，當知無量。一者、由時分分別。謂於墮在過去、未來及現在世一切所知，隨悟入故。二者、由品類分別。謂於一一諸有為事自相、共相一切行相，隨悟入故。三者、由相續分別。謂於十方一切有情界各各差別一切相續一切事義，隨悟入故。即由如是三種分別，如來十力當知無量。是名如來十力分別。
items.en:
Second, differentiation; first, raising the question. What is the differentiation of the Tathāgata's ten powers?
Second, briefly stating. In brief, through three kinds of differentiation, they should be known as immeasurable.
Third, listing and explaining; first, differentiation by time. First, differentiation by time: penetrating and comprehending everything knowable falling within the past, future, and present.
Second, differentiation by kind. Second, differentiation by kind: penetrating and comprehending the specific and shared characteristics of every conditioned phenomenon.
Third, differentiation by continuity. Third, differentiation by continuity: penetrating and comprehending every distinct being's own continuity and every matter pertaining to it, throughout every direction.
Fourth, concluding overall. Through these three kinds of differentiation, the Tathāgata's ten powers should be known as immeasurable; this is called the differentiation of the Tathāgata's ten powers.

items.title: Section: The Third and Fourth Angles — Belonging to the Buddha Alone, Yet Equally Shared by Every Buddha

items.zh: 云何如來十力不共？謂唯如來有此十力，不共一切聲聞、獨覺。是名如來十力不共。云何如來十力平等？謂此十力，一切如來悉皆平等具足成就，故說平等無有差別。若就如來多所安住，是則如來如是十力展轉差別。謂餘如來多住餘力，其餘如來復住餘力。是名如來十力平等。
items.en:
Third, exclusivity. What makes the Tathāgata's ten powers exclusive? Only the Tathāgata possesses these ten powers, shared with no śrāvaka or pratyekabuddha; this is called the exclusivity of the Tathāgata's ten powers.
Fourth, equality; first, posing the question. What is the equality of the Tathāgata's ten powers?
Second, explaining; first, equal attainment without difference. These ten powers are equally and completely accomplished by every Tathāgata; hence they are said to be equal, without difference.
Second, a difference in predominant abiding. Yet with respect to which power a Tathāgata dwells in most, there is indeed a difference among Tathāgatas accordingly: one Tathāgata dwells predominantly in one power, another Tathāgata dwells predominantly in another.
Third, concluding. This is called the equality of the Tathāgata's ten powers.

items.title: Section: The Fifth Angle Opens — What Each of the First Six Powers Actually Accomplishes

items.zh: 云何如來十力作業？謂如來所有處非處智力，於諸因中如實知因，於諸果中如實知果；及能降伏無因、惡因種種諍論，一切沙門、婆羅門等。如來所有自業智力，於自所作受用果業如實了知；及能降伏施福移轉種種諍論，一切沙門、婆羅門等。如來所有靜慮、解脫、等持、等至智力，能現三種神變，無到教授所化有情；及能降伏安住種種相違異品怨害諍論，一切沙門、婆羅門等。如來所有根勝劣智力，於諸有情軟中上根部分差別如實了知，及能於彼如應如宜為說正法。如來所有種種勝解智力，於諸有情軟中上品、淨與不淨勝解差別如實了知；其淨勝解令漸增長，不淨勝解令漸捨離。如來所有種種界智力，於諸有情劣中妙界部分差別如實了知；於諸有情能如其根、如其意樂、如其隨眠，依於彼彼趣入門中，無倒教授，如應安立。
items.en:
Fifth, function; first, posing the question. What is the function of the Tathāgata's ten powers?
Second, explaining; first, the power of wisdom regarding what is possible and impossible. The Tathāgata's power of wisdom regarding what is possible and impossible truly knows cause as cause and fruit as fruit within every cause; and it subdues every rival argument of no cause or false cause among all ascetics and brahmins.
Second, the power of wisdom regarding karma. The Tathāgata's power of wisdom regarding karma truly knows the karma one performs and the fruit one experiences by one's own action; and it subdues every rival argument of transferring the merit of giving among all ascetics and brahmins.
Third, the power of wisdom regarding meditative absorptions, liberations, equipoise, and attainment. The Tathāgata's power of wisdom regarding these can manifest three kinds of miraculous transformation, teaching the beings to be transformed without distortion; and it subdues every rival argument rooted in mutually hostile, contradictory positions among all ascetics and brahmins.
Fourth, the power of wisdom regarding superior and inferior faculties. The Tathāgata's power of wisdom regarding superior and inferior faculties truly knows the distinctions among beings' inferior, middling, and superior faculties, and accordingly teaches the true dharma exactly as is fitting.
Fifth, the power of wisdom regarding various resolute inclinations. The Tathāgata's power of wisdom regarding various resolute inclinations truly knows the distinctions among beings' inferior, middling, and superior, pure or impure resolute understanding; pure understanding is caused to grow gradually, impure understanding is gradually abandoned.
Sixth, the power of wisdom regarding various elements; first, briefly stating what corresponds. The Tathāgata's power of wisdom regarding various elements truly knows the distinctions among beings' inferior, middling, and excellent elements; and according to each being's faculties, inclinations, and latent tendencies, in whatever gateway of practice they are entering, it provides undistorted instruction, established as is fitting.

items.title: Section: Teaching Śrāvakas in Full, and the Eleven Provisions a Bodhisattva Needs Before Settling the Mind

items.zh: 此中如來為諸聲聞，依於彼彼趣入門中與正教授，如聲聞地盡一切種無間宣說、顯發、辯了、施設、開示。云何如來教授一切始業、初業、等持資糧攝受安住欲住其心諸菩薩眾，令心得住？
items.en:
Second, teaching in detail; first, for śrāvakas. Here, the Tathāgata provides correct instruction to śrāvakas according to whatever gateway of practice each is entering, exactly as explained without interruption throughout the Śrāvaka Ground — revealing, clarifying, formulating, and disclosing.
Second, for bodhisattvas; first, posing the question. How does the Tathāgata instruct all the beginning, newly embarked bodhisattvas gathering the provisions for meditative equipoise, wishing to settle their own minds, so that their minds become settled?

items.title: Section: "Reflect on the Name Your Parents Gave You" — Contemplating the Self Through the Six Sense Bases

items.zh: 謂諸如來為無諂曲、恭敬愛重，等持資糧、始業、初業諸菩薩眾，最初施設無倒教授。如是告言：善男子來！汝當安處遠離臥具獨一無二，於內寂靜如理思惟汝之父母所為立名，或汝親教軌範師等所為立名。如是思惟：我今為有離六處法自性真實，或內、或外、或兩中間，於此有中，如是名想施設假立言說轉耶？汝既如是正思惟已，當於此法都無所得。
items.en:
Second, explaining; first, establishing instruction; first, briefly stating. The Tathāgatas, for bodhisattvas free of flattery and deception, reverent and cherishing the provisions for meditative equipoise, whether beginners or newly embarked, first establish undistorted instruction.
Second, direct address; first, properly reflecting; first, on one's own name; first, stating the reflection. Thus it is said: "Come, good son! You should dwell in a secluded resting place, alone and undivided, inwardly tranquil, and properly reflect, as is fitting, upon the name your parents gave you, or the name given by your preceptor or instructing teacher."
Second, explaining the manner of the reflection. Reflect thus: "Is there, apart from the six sense-bases, some truly real, essential self — whether within, without, or in between — to which this name, this notion, this provisional designation and manner of speech, actually refers?"
Third, presenting the resulting understanding. "Having thus properly reflected, you should find that nothing at all corresponding to this can be found."

blocks.text: Fascicle 50 is the last of the Bodhisattva Ground. It opens by looking at the ten powers from seven angles. Inside the discussion is a short, practical meditation: reflect on the name your parents gave you.
Nature, differentiation, exclusivity, equality, function, sequence, and distinction. Venerable Miào Jìng: master these seven and you master the essentials of the ten powers.
"In general, the five faculties constitute their nature; but because wisdom is foremost, it is said that wisdom is the nature of the ten powers."
By time, by kind, and by continuity. Venerable Miào Jìng: continuity means the body, changing yet continuous.

Master Cháng Bǎi: because the conditions for teaching differ, each buddha's abiding differs. Venerable Miào Jìng: Śākyamuni, for example, may dwell mostly in the power regarding the possible and impossible.

The first subdues arguments of no cause or false cause. Venerable Miào Jìng: false cause means treating wrongdoing as a cause of good, or claiming one person's merit passes to another. Master Cháng Bǎi: merit cannot be bought or transferred; one cultivates it oneself.

Venerable Miào Jìng: the provisions for one beginning practice are precepts, guarding the senses, moderation in food, less sleep, and awareness. Master Cháng Bǎi: like preparing a car for a long drive.

One reflects on the name given by parents or teachers. Master Cháng Bǎi: a name is only a label for this life, a convenience for communication. Venerable Miào Jìng: there is no self in the six sense bases, nor apart from them.
Try the treatise's exercise: say your own name silently, and ask what it refers to. The eye? The body? Something apart from them? Tomorrow's passage continues the meditation.

quiz.q: Through which seven characteristics are the ten powers synthesised?
options: nature, differentiation, exclusivity, equality, function, sequence, distinction
hearing, reflection, cultivation, discipline, concentration, wisdom, liberation
quiz.why: Nature, differentiation, exclusivity, equality, function, sequence, and distinction. Master Cháng Bǎi: seven angles on the ten powers. Venerable Miào Jìng: master these seven and you master the essentials of the ten powers.

quiz.q: What does the treatise give as the nature of the ten powers?
options: the five faculties together; because wisdom is foremost, wisdom is named
quiz.why: "In general, the five faculties constitute their nature; but because wisdom is foremost, it is said that wisdom is the nature of the ten powers."

quiz.q: Among the three undefiled faculties, to which do both lecturers assign the ten powers?
options: the faculty of coming to know
the faculty of one who has fully known
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the nature of the ten powers falls under the last of the three, the faculty of one who has fully known. Venerable Miào Jìng says the same.

quiz.q: Through which three differentiations are the powers immeasurable?
quiz.why: Differentiation by time, by kind, and by continuity. Venerable Miào Jìng: kind concerns conditioned things; continuity means the body, changing yet continuous.

quiz.q: If all buddhas are equal in the powers, whence the difference in predominant abiding? What do the lectures say?
options: attainment is equal, abiding differs — Cháng Bǎi: conditions of teaching beings differ; Miào Jìng: Śākyamuni may dwell mostly in the first power
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: because the conditions of teaching beings differ, each buddha's abiding differs. Venerable Miào Jìng: Śākyamuni, for example, may dwell mostly in the power regarding the possible and impossible.

quiz.q: Which rival arguments does the first power subdue?
quiz.why: It subdues arguments of no cause or false cause. Venerable Miào Jìng: false cause means treating wrongdoing as a cause of good.

quiz.q: What is the claim of "transferring the merit of giving," and how does the power of karma refute it?
options: merit goes only to the receiver
one's karmic merit jumps to another; Cháng Bǎi: merit can't be traded — one must cultivate it
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: the claim that one person's merit passes to another. Master Cháng Bǎi: merit can't be bought or transferred; one cultivates it oneself.

quiz.q: The third power manifests three miraculous transformations. Why does the Buddha show them, says Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: so beings revere him and listen attentively
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: showing powers makes beings revere the Buddha, so they listen attentively.

quiz.q: How do the lectures explain "beginning, newly embarked" bodhisattvas with the provisions for equipoise?
options: they differ: Miào Jìng: 初業 is starting practice, provisions are precepts, sense-guarding, etc.; Cháng Bǎi: 始業 first practises the nine stages of settling, with the road-trip simile
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: 初業 is beginning to practise; precepts, sense-guarding, moderation in food, less sleep, and awareness are the provisions. Master Cháng Bǎi: 始業 first practises the nine stages of settling; like preparing a car for a long drive.

quiz.q: What does the Tathāgata tell beginners to reflect on first?
options: the name given by one's parents or teachers
quiz.why: One reflects on the name given by parents or teachers. Master Cháng Bǎi: a name is only a label for this life-form, a convenience for communication.

quiz.q: The English merges "apart from the six sense-bases… within, without, or between" into one question. How do the lectures read it?
options: Miào Jìng: 真實 means indestructible; no self in or apart from the six bases; Cháng Bǎi: life is only bases and consciousnesses working together
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: no self in the six bases, nor apart from them — two steps the English merges. Master Cháng Bǎi: life is the combined working of inner bases, outer bases, and six consciousnesses.
